analysis.note: Temporal adverb; the bhāṣya glosses it with tadānīm.
Genitive singular: “of the seer.” The bhāṣya names the referent as citi, consciousness; the supplied line reads citi without final visarga, likely for/standing in place of citiḥ.
Locative singular, construed with avasthānam: “in its own form/nature.”

verification.detail: compound stem svarūpa as Napumsaka/Saptami/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Neuter nominative singular abstract noun. The form is also accusative by shape, but the bhāṣya’s nominal gloss pratiṣṭhā supports a nominative state/predicate: “abiding/being established.”

justifications.chosen: tadā means “then, at that time,” not primarily “therefore.”

evidence.translation: At that time, consciousness is established in its own form/nature.

justifications.decision: Referent and technical force of draṣṭuḥ.
justifications.chosen: draṣṭṛ is the seer as consciousness (citi), not an ordinary empirical observer.

evidence.translation: At that time, consciousness is established in its own form/nature. The supplied text has citi; it is understood as the consciousness named by the gloss.

justifications.decision: Case construal of svarūpe and its relation to avasthānam.
options_considered: locative complement: abiding/being established in its own nature
loose adverbial: while in its own form
physical location: in its own shape/body
justifications.chosen: svarūpe is the locative complement of avasthānam: “in its own form/nature.”

options_considered: accusative object of an omitted verb
justifications.chosen: avasthānam is an abstract nominal state, “abiding/being established,” syntactically nominative in the elliptical sūtra.

options_considered: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa sense: svasya rūpam, “form of oneself”
justifications.chosen: svarūpa is analyzed as a karmadhāraya compound: svaṃ rūpam, “one’s own form/nature.”

translation: Then: the seer’s (draṣṭṛ)—consciousness’s (citi)—abiding (avasthāna) in its own nature (svarūpa).
one_shot_delta: Without the bhāṣya, one might translate draṣṭṛ as an ordinary “viewer”; Vyāsa’s gloss points to citi, consciousness, as the seer.
A commentary-blind rendering might make avasthānam mere “residence” or “standing”; the gloss svarūpapratiṣṭhā gives “being established in its own nature.”
The adverb tadā could be over-read as inferential “therefore”; the bhāṣya’s tadānīm supports the temporal “then/at that time.”
open_questions: The supplied bhāṣya line ends citi without final visarga; it has been quoted verbatim and understood as referring to citiḥ, consciousness.
